tool.name: google_developer_search
tool.description: Searches and retrieves official Google developer documentation, product guides, API references, code samples, and tutorials. Use this tool whenever the user asks a question about any Google technology, product, service, API, SDK, or development pattern — including Android, Firebase, Google Cloud (GCP), Gemini, Google Maps, Google Workspace, BigQuery, Cloud Run, Vertex AI, Flutter, Kotlin, Google Identity, Pub/Sub, or any developers.google.com or cloud.google.com content. Returns structured content including article text, titles, and canonical URLs.

invoke_when: User asks how to configure, set up, or use any Google product or service
User asks what a Google technology is or how it works
User asks for code examples related to any Google SDK, API, or library
User asks about Android, Firebase, Google Cloud, Gemini, Google Maps, Google Workspace, BigQuery, Cloud Run, Vertex AI, Flutter, or Kotlin
User asks about Google Identity, OAuth with Google, Google Sign-In, or Firebase Authentication
User asks a follow-up question that requires additional Google developer documentation
do_not_invoke_when: The user's question is purely about a Microsoft or non-Google technology
The retrieved content from the current session already covers the user's follow-up question

session_management.note: Persist the Google MCP session ID across conversation turns. Pass it on every subsequent tool call to maintain server-side context and avoid re-initialisation overhead on each turn.

deduplication.note: Before passing results to the agent for rendering, normalise all returned URLs (strip trailing slashes, lowercase scheme and host, remove tracking parameters: utm_*, hl, tab). Suppress any result whose normalised URL already appeared in a prior turn of this session.

source_rendering.note: Sources must NEVER be rendered as a visible list, raw URL block, or Sources section. The most relevant retrieved URL surfaces exclusively as the final line of the agent response in the format: [See more: Article Title](canonical_url). Only one closing line per turn. If no valid URL was retrieved, the closing line is omitted.
